content:
Then answered him Agamemnon, lord of men:
"Rejoice, son of Laertes, godlike Odysseus, at this speech of yours,
for all things you have ordered are just and well arranged.
As for me, I am willing to swear this oath, and my spirit urges me on,
and I will not perjure myself before the god. But let Achilles
remain by his ships, eager for war as he is.
190 And let all the rest of you stay here until the gifts are brought
from my hut and we swear binding oaths.
But you—for you I now command and charge—
choose the best and bravest of the Achaeans,
and bring to my ship the gifts we yesterday agreed to give to Achilles
195 and the woman as well. Let Talthybius quickly
go through the wide Achaean host
and prepare a boar for sacrifice to Zeus and to Helios."
